lines.text: The spirit of Mayor Nagin's One New Orleans prioritizes accountability, responsibility, transparency and
inclusion in all levels of government for the benefit of all citizens. As we enter our 3rd year of recovery
and rebuilding, we as citizens must rethink old practices and be creative and innovative in our recovery
strategies; renew our commitment to a fullrecovery for everyone; revive the spirit of this great city, and
as a result, this year's budget embraces and advances the Citywide Strategic Recovery and
Redevelopment Plan - the people's plan -- for our rebuilding. The city has focused initial recovery
The people's plan is based on the Unified New Orleans Plan (UNOP), which involved the development of
13 district plans by people living in those neighborhoods with support from top national planning firms.
The Unified Plan engaged citizens in New Orleans and the diaspora in unprecedented levels of public
participation throughout its process. The final recommendations received resounding support in the third
and final Community Congress meeting of more than 1,300 citizens in four cities throughout the country.
Recovery planning began when Mayor Nagin convened the Bring New Orleans Back Commission 30 days
after Katrina's landfall. Key areas for the commission were land use, flood protection, public transit,
culture, education, healthcare and economic development and governmental effectiveness. The
commission gave its final presentation in December 2005, four months after the storm.
